title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (archive page 678). The previous page explains the problem. A group scheme Z~ over S_0 = Spec Z, which parametrizes 'automorphism-like' data (μ, α_0, β_0), has an exceptional fibre of larger dimension in characteristic 3. The cause is that in characteristic 3 the curve C_K has more automorphisms than in other characteristics. This fits the j = 0 = 1728 elliptic curve, whose automorphism group has order 12 in characteristic 3 instead of 6; the O_12^* on the next page points the same way. Grothendieck does not try to repair this by ad hoc redefinitions. Instead he cuts out a closed subgroup scheme N ⊂ Z~ that is smooth over Spec Z and agrees with Z~ over Z[1/3].

What this page does, step by step.

1. Let M be a rank-2 lattice with basis λ_0, λ_1. The data fit M = Z[ω], the Eisenstein integers, with ρ acting as multiplication by a cube root of unity.

2. Define (99): M_0 = {c_0 λ_0 + c_1 λ_1 | c_0 + c_1 ≡ 0 mod 3}. This is the index-3 sublattice, which is exactly the image (1-ω)M of 1 - ρ. Check: (1-ω)(a + bω) = (a+b) + (2b-a)ω, whose coefficient sum is 3b. It gives a vector bundle (vector group) M_0 underlined over S_0.

3. The cocycle map (100), Z~_{ρ,σ} → M_0, is (μ, α_0, β_0) ↦ (1-ρ_μ)(α~_0) + (1-σ_μ)(β_0), where α~_0 = α_0 ± ν''(λ_1 - λ_0). Note that λ_1 - λ_0 = ω - 1 already lies in M_0.

4. This map is obtained by first building an honest Z-linear map (101), M × M × Z → M_0, then passing to the associated module schemes (102), M × M × G_a → M_0, and composing with (103), (μ, α_0, β_0) ↦ (α_0, β_0, ν''(μ)).

5. Conclusion of the page: the cocycle equation (96) can be read as an equation in M_0 rather than in M, and is thereby 'stricter'.

What the next page completes. Solvability of (96) in M_0 defines a closed subscheme N_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Z~. Its map to O_12^* is surjective, with fibres given by the kernel of the linear map (106), M × M → M_0, (α~, β) ↦ (1-ρ)α~ - (1-σ)β. That map is a surjective Z-linear map of lattices, so the induced map of vector groups is a smooth epimorphism. Hence N is smooth over Spec Z.

In modern terms: the failure of flatness or smoothness comes from the cokernel of 1 - ρ on M ⊗ F_3, since M/(1-ω)M ≅ F_3. Replacing the target lattice by the image lattice M_0 makes the defining linear map surjective integrally. This yields a smooth integral model, in the spirit of a Néron-type smoothening or a dilatation-like replacement.
errors: (99) is transcribed 'M_0 = M'; it must mean M_0 ⊂ M (index-3 sublattice), with the defining set below (the '‖ dfn' is a definitional equality to the set).

For (101) to land in M_0, the term (1-σ_M)(β_0) must lie in M_0. This requires σ to act trivially on M/M_0 ≅ F_3, for instance σ a power of ω. If σ were -1 (order 2), then 1-σ = 2 and the image would not lie in M_0. The page does not justify this, and it depends on what σ is in §§ 49-50/96.
The sign '±' in front of ν''(λ_1 - λ_0) is left undetermined in the manuscript.

Smoothness of N (next page) needs flatness of N → O_12^* fibrewise as torsors under a smooth kernel. This is asserted ('il est clair') rather than proved; it is plausible because the kernel of a surjective map of vector groups coming from a surjective lattice map is a smooth vector group.

ideas.what: Replace the target lattice M by the image sublattice M_0 = (1-ω)M of index 3, so that the cocycle (linear) map becomes surjective over Z and the associated map of vector groups is a smooth epimorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Smooth integral model / cutting out a smooth closed subgroup scheme (Néron-type smoothening, dilatation-like construction); cokernel of 1-ρ as obstruction at p=3
ideas.where_published: Not in this specific form; general smoothness criteria are in EGA IV / SGA 3

ideas.what: Extra automorphisms of the j=0 elliptic curve in characteristic 3 causing a jump in fibre dimension of a group scheme of automorphism/cocycle data over Spec Z
ideas.modern_name: Non-flatness at p=3 of automorphism group schemes of elliptic curves (Aut of order 12 in char 3)

ideas.what: Passing from a Z-linear map of lattices to a homomorphism of the associated vector group schemes over Spec Z (M ↦ underlined M), using the target Z ↦ G_a.
ideas.modern_name: Vector group scheme V(M) associated with a lattice

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine technical step. It defines an index-3 sublattice equal to the image of 1-ρ on the Eisenstein lattice, and rereads a cocycle equation there to get a smooth closed subgroup scheme over Z. Correct in spirit and standard technique; nothing new to specialists.
